answer: For a vault-access poll, a museum admits domains publishing a ferrous relic catalogue. A registrar checks catalogue eligibility and a fresh DNS challenge, then signs credentials bound to the registered domain and poll. Validators reject invalid signatures and repeated domains, including reissues; subdomains add no votes. Extra influence requires controlling more registered domains and publishing qualifying catalogues. Sequential reuse adds nothing within this poll. Cheap domains and copied catalogues can make capture easy; this trusts the registrar.
